commit.message:
feat(ErdosProblems/1191): add Erdős Problem 1191 (#7167)

Adds [Erdős Problem 1191](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1191) ([Er80, p.
98]), the $1000 problem on the lower growth of infinite Sidon sets. The
page asks two questions and both are open:

- `parts.i`: for every infinite Sidon set A, is liminf |A ∩ [1, x]| /
x^(1/2) · (log x)^(1/2) = 0?
- `parts.ii`: is there an infinite Sidon set A and some c > 0 with
liminf |A ∩ [1, x]| / x^(1/2) · (log x)^c > 0?

It also adds the result the page attributes to Erdős (see Halberstam and
Roth, Sequences, 1966) as `variants.liminf_le`: for every infinite Sidon
set the same liminf with exponent 1/2 is at most some constant c > 0.

Formalisation choices:

- The liminf is taken in `ℝ≥0∞` through `ENNReal.ofReal`, as in
`erdos_158.variants.isSidon'`. In `ℝ`, `liminf` of a sequence that tends
to infinity is 0, which would make `parts.i` easier to satisfy than
intended. In `ℝ≥0∞` that case gives ⊤, and in `parts.ii` a liminf of ⊤
correctly counts as positive.
- x runs over ℕ instead of ℝ. Between consecutive integers the count is
constant and x^(-1/2) (log x)^c changes by a factor tending to 1, so the
liminf is the same.
- The count is `(A ∩ Set.Icc 1 x).ncard` to match A ∩ [1, x] on the
page, as in 39.lean. Sidon uses `IsSidon` from ForMathlib.
- In `variants.liminf_le` the constant may depend on A, so the statement
is equivalent to the liminf being finite. This is the weaker reading of
"for some constant c > 0". It is the same result as
`erdos_158.variants.isSidon'`, restated with this problem's count A ∩
[1, x], and the docstring points there. I kept the `∃ c` form because it
is how the page states it. I could not check in Halberstam and Roth
whether Erdős's constant is absolute. If it is, the `∃ c` can move in
front of the `∀ A`.

Not included: the remark that Erdős may have meant the optimal f with
liminf |A ∩ [1, x]| / x^(1/2) · f(x) = 0 for all infinite Sidon sets,
since the page only guesses at it. The page also says "See also [729]
for the behaviour of the limsup", but problem 729 is about prime factors
of n!/(a!b!). The limsup question for Sidon sets is problem 329, so this
looks like a typo on the site and I left it out of the docstring.

I searched for an existing issue or PR for this problem and did not find
one.

`lake --wfail build 'FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«1191»'` passes
with no warnings.

Update: main has dropped `answer(...)`, so I merged main and rewrote the
statements in the new form, tagged `question`, with `¬` in front where
the answer is no.

AI-usage disclosure: Claude (Anthropic) was minorly used to assist in
drafting the Lean statement.

+-/
+module
+
+public import FormalConjecturesUtil
+
+/-!
+# Erdős Problem 1191
+
+*References:*
+- [erdosproblems.com/1191](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1191)
+- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math.
+  (1980), 89-115.
+- [HaRo66] Halberstam, H. and Roth, K. F., *Sequences. Vol. I*. (1966), xx+291.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+open Filter Real
+
+namespace Erdos1191
+
+/--
+Let $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ be an infinite Sidon set. Is it true that
+$$\liminf_{x\to \infty} \frac{\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert}{x^{1/2}}(\log x)^{1/2}=0?$$
+
+Here $x$ runs over $\mathbb{N}$ and the $\liminf$ is taken in `ℝ≥0∞`, so that it is $\infty$
+rather than $0$ when the sequence tends to infinity.
+-/
+@[category research open, question, AMS 5 11]
+theorem erdos_1191.parts.i : ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite → IsSidon A →
+    liminf (fun x : ℕ ↦ ENNReal.ofReal
+      ((A ∩ .Icc 1 x).ncard / (x : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ) * log x ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ))) atTop = 0 := by
+  sorry
+
+/--
+Does there exist an infinite Sidon set $A$ such that
+$$\liminf_{x\to \infty} \frac{\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert}{x^{1/2}}(\log x)^c>0$$
+for some $c>0$?
+
+A positive answer would also give a positive answer to Erdős Problem 39.
+-/
+@[category research open, question, AMS 5 11]
+theorem erdos_1191.parts.ii : ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ IsSidon A ∧
+    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), 0 < liminf (fun x : ℕ ↦ ENNReal.ofReal
+      ((A ∩ .Icc 1 x).ncard / (x : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ) * log x ^ c)) atTop := by
+  sorry
+
+/--
+Erdős proved (see for example [HaRo66]) that if $A$ is an infinite Sidon set then
+$$\liminf_{x\to \infty} \frac{\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert}{x^{1/2}}(\log x)^{1/2}\leq c$$
+for some constant $c>0$. See also `erdos_158.variants.isSidon'`.
+-/
+@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
+theorem erdos_1191.variants.liminf_le {A : Set ℕ} (hAinf : A.Infinite) (hAsid : IsSidon A) :
+    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), liminf (fun x : ℕ ↦ ENNReal.ofReal
+      ((A ∩ .Icc 1 x).ncard / (x : ℝ) ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ) * log x ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ))) atTop ≤
+        ENNReal.ofReal c := by
+  sorry
+
+end Erdos1191
